title: Ταὼς καὶ κολοιός
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 334. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Τῶν ὀρνέων βουλευομένων περὶ βασιλείας, ταὼς ἠξίου αὐτὸν χειροτονῆσαι βασιλέα διὰ τὸ κάλλος.
sentences.tr: Tōn orneōn bouleuomenōn peri basileias, taōs ēxiou auton cheirotonēsai basilea dia to kallos.
sentences.l: The birds deliberating about kingship, the peacock was claiming that they should elect him king on account of his beauty.
sentences.i: When the birds were deliberating about the kingship, the peacock claimed that they ought to elect him king for his beauty.
sentences.n: A genitive absolute (τῶν ὀρνέων βουλευομένων) sets the scene before the main clause — the fable's regular way of opening. ἀξιόω with the infinitive is to claim a thing as one's due. χειροτονέω is to elect by show of hands, the Athenian assembly's method of voting, and the word keeps that picture.

sentences.t: Ὡρμημένων δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦτο τῶν ὀρνέων, κολοιὸς εἶπεν· « Ἀλλ’ ἐάν, σοῦ βασιλεύοντος, ἀετὸς ἡμᾶς διώκῃ, πῶς ἡμῖν ἐπαρκέσεις ; »
sentences.tr: Hōrmēmenōn de epi touto tōn orneōn, koloios eipen· « All’ ean, sou basileuontos, aetos hēmas diōkēi, pōs hēmin eparkeseis ; »
sentences.l: And the birds being already set upon this, a jackdaw said: « But if, with you reigning, an eagle pursues us, how will you help us? »
sentences.i: But when the birds were already bent on it, a jackdaw said: « And if an eagle chases us while you are king, how will you defend us? »
sentences.n: Two genitive absolutes in one sentence: ὡρμημένων … τῶν ὀρνέων outside the speech, σοῦ βασιλεύοντος inside it. ὥρμημαι is a perfect middle of ὁρμάω, 'to have set oneself in motion towards', hence 'be bent on'. ἐπαρκέω, 'be a defence to', takes the dative.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι οὐ μεμπτοὶ ὅσοι προειδότες τοὺς μέλλοντας κινδύνους, πρὶν παθεῖν, φυλάττονται.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti ou memptoi hosoi proeidotes tous mellontas kindynous, prin pathein, phylattontai.
sentences.l: The story shows that not blameworthy are those who, foreseeing the coming dangers, guard themselves before suffering.
sentences.i: The story shows that those are not to be blamed who foresee the dangers to come and are on their guard before they suffer.
sentences.n: μεμπτός is a verbal adjective, 'to be found fault with'; the copula is left unexpressed, as often in these morals. προειδότες is the perfect participle of πρόοιδα, which like οἶδα has present force. πρίν takes the bare infinitive when the main clause is affirmative.
